panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Radiograph of the hand showing changes consistent with fight bite-induced septic joint, as part of the diagnostic series. B: Radiograph of the hand showing changes consistent with fight bite-induced septic joint, as part of the diagnostic series. C: Close-up radiograph of the right MCP joint showing bony effacement and periosteal elevation, diagnostic features of fight bite induced osteomyelitis.

in_text_mentions: X-rays of the hand (figure 2) revealed changes consistent with osteomyelitis of the fourth metacarpal head, showcased by effacement of the lateral aspects of the bony head along with a focal point of periosteal elevation. The patient was admitted, and a subsequent ultrasound of the fourth finger and MCP joint demonstrated moderate flexor and extensor tenosynovitis of the ring finger, along with synovitis of the metacarpophalangeal joint and no drainable effusion.

Our patient developed progressive infection with deterioration of extensor and flexor tendon sheaths along with bone, as evidenced by features of osteomyelitis on X-ray (see Figure 2). Periosteal elevation, loss of articular surface, and smoothened cortex of bone are common radiographic features of bony degradation from osteomyelitis [15].
